value: organic Rankine cycle: an organic working fluid with a lower boiling point than water drives a turbine on waste heat; can be sized economically in sub-MW packages and run with air-cooled condensers and unattended
steam Rankine cycle: waste heat boiler raising steam for a condensing steam turbine; the most common WHP system in the US and the most familiar to industry

Kalina cycle: Rankine cycle on an ammonia-water mixture; 15-25% more efficient than an ORC at the same temperature and highest theoretical efficiency, but complex, so suited to systems of several MW or more

note: more common overseas in geothermal plants; SRC and ORC are much more prevalent in the US
